name: Diario de Obras
tagline: Daily site log for construction work: entries, photos and incidents per project, exported as dated reports.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is embarrassingly simple: projects, dated entries, free text, photos, weather, crew count, and a PDF at the end of the month. An agent will produce a working version of that in a single sitting, and for a solo builder or small contractor it will genuinely do the job. What it will not produce in one sitting is the part that matters on a muddy site: a real mobile app that captures photos offline at 7am with no signal, syncs when it reconnects, and never loses an entry. Add to that the fact that a site diary is often a semi-legal document, with format expectations from clients, architects or insurers, and that signed, timestamped, tamper-evident records are the whole reason anyone keeps one. Buildable, but the field-grade version is a weekend minimum and the evidentiary version is not a weekend at all.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create projects, add dated log entries with photos, notes, weather and crew, and export a date-range PDF report per project.
requirements: Node runtime on a laptop or small VPS
Local disk or S3-compatible bucket for photos
A phone browser for on-site capture, PWA install if you want it offline-ish
Your own backup routine, because site logs are the thing you least want to lose
whatYouLose: Offline-first native capture with reliable background sync when the signal comes back
Photo handling at scale: EXIF stripping decisions, GPS stamps, thumbnails, storage that does not fill your disk
Report formats that clients, architects and insurers already recognise without argument
Shared access for crew, site manager and client with sane permissions
Tamper-evidence: immutable timestamps, signatures, an audit trail that holds up in a dispute
moatNotes: The moat is not the schema, it is working reliably with wet gloves, bad signal and a client who wants the PDF to look official.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a site diary only has value if it is complete and trusted, and both of those are operational problems rather than coding problems. Contractors pay so that the photo taken at the far end of a basement with no bars still exists next Tuesday, so that the monthly report prints in a shape the architect accepts, and so that when a dispute arrives in eighteen months there is a dated, consistent record rather than a folder of phone pictures. A self-built version solves the data entry and skips all of that, which is fine right up until the one day it is not.
notes: The CRUD is a Saturday; the trust is the product.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted construction site diary web app. Single operator, no multi-tenant accounts.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, server actions only, no separate API layer.
- SQLite via Drizzle ORM, file at ./data/diary.db, migrations committed.
- Tailwind for styling. No component library.
- Photos stored on local disk at ./data/photos, served through a route handler. Resize to max 1600px wide with sharp, keep the original too.
- PDF export with @react-pdf/renderer, rendered server side.
- Installable PWA: manifest, icons, service worker that caches the app shell. Do not attempt full offline write sync.

Data model:
- project: id, name, client, address, startDate, status (active | closed), notes.
- entry: id, projectId, date, weather (text), temperature (nullable), crewCount, hoursWorked, workDone (long text), incidents (long text, nullable), materialsDelivered (text, nullable), createdAt, lockedAt (nullable).
- photo: id, entryId, filename, caption, takenAt, sortOrder.

Features in scope:
- Project list and project detail with a reverse-chronological entry timeline.
- Mobile-first entry form, big touch targets, date defaults to today, multi-photo upload straight from the camera input with per-photo captions.
- Lock an entry: sets lockedAt, makes it read-only in the UI, records a SHA-256 hash of the entry text plus photo filenames in a separate append-only ledger table. Be clear in the README that this is tamper-evident, not legally tamper-proof.
- Date-range PDF report per project: cover page with project details, one page per entry with photos in a 2-up grid, page numbers and a generated-on footer.
- CSV export of all entries.
- Full-text search across workDone and incidents using SQLite FTS5.
- A single shared password from AUTH_PASSWORD in .env, cookie session, nothing more.

Out of scope, do not build: user roles, client portals, invoicing, Gantt charts, cloud storage, email, telemetry, analytics, any third-party API.

Deliver a README with setup, a backup command that tars ./data, and an honest limitations section covering offline capture and legal admissibility.
